rows.title: Ages posted in the wrong unit: mostly a negative
rows.claim: Ages posted in the wrong unit: mostly a negative. Re-fetched 2026-11-24: 396 baseline age means in 157 trials sit outside the trial's own age limits. Reading them as months, weeks or days does not beat decoy factors: against an unflagged arm of the same trial, months fit 3 groups and /10 and /24 fit 3 each; among the 24 trials whose limits are posted in months, weeks or days, `registry.py units` (mean inside and SD under the Bhatia-Davis cap, both converted) fits 15 in the limits' own unit, but /10 and /24 fit 13 each, because infant age windows are wide. Only narrow windows separate them, and there three trials fit months and nothing else of 12 factors bar one: NCT00847145 (365 to 394 days, 12.3 "years"), NCT00984295 (12 to 15 months, 12.4), NCT06026124 (48 to 71 months, 59.13); all three re-fetched live and match. The SD rule also removed a false lead: NCT03071575's 26.5 (SD 5.4) fits as weeks but no SD of 5.4 weeks fits a 14-day window, so it reads as the mothers' ages. Most other flags are adolescent trials whose means of 30 to 50 are parents.
rows.level: observed (3 cases); the rule itself has no signal over decoys
rows.check: decoy factors; peer arms; SD cap; 3 live re-fetches
rows.literature: unit errors are known in general; no registry count found
rows.status: closed as a rule; 3 cases worth a note to the registry

rows.title: Alcohols counted with and without stereoisomers
rows.claim: Alcohols counted with and without stereoisomers. Letting a carbon's three slots only rotate (the group C3 in place of S3) gives A000625, and a centroid formula under A4 gives stereo alkanes, A000628. Observed, reproduced from the literature: all three match their OEIS b-files, A000598 and A000625 to 100 carbons and A000628 over its 38 published terms, and explicit trees agree to 12 carbons for the two alcohol series. At 100 carbons stereoisomers multiply the alcohol count about 3.6 million times.

rows.title: Three people sharing a birthday
rows.claim: Three people sharing a birthday. A direct count over how many dates hold a pair and a one-person-at-a-time Markov chain agree as exact fractions for every group up to 120. The smallest group past a half is 88 at 0.51107, and 87 falls short at 0.49945. Observed, reproduced from the literature: 88 is the published value.

rows.title: Pigeonhole formulas up to 6 holes are unsatisfiable under DPLL, confirmed by exhaustive assignment to 3 holes
rows.claim: Pigeonhole formulas up to 6 holes are unsatisfiable under DPLL, confirmed by exhaustive assignment to 3 holes. With this branching order the search takes 1, 3, 11, 47, 239 and 1439 nodes, which is 2 h! - 1 at every size tried. Observed only, for one branching order, not a theorem. Largest prime gaps in five disjoint windows of 90,000 starting at 10^3, 10^5, 10^6, 10^7 and 10^8: 72 at 31397, 86 at 155921, 90 at 1053863, 120 at 10052071, 168 at 100058683, each with both ends proved prime and every number between proved composite by trial division.

rows.title: Step 4 of the triangular ground-state proof, its weakest link, now has an independent machine check for n = 2…
rows.claim: Step 4 of the triangular ground-state proof, its weakest link, now has an independent machine check for n = 2 to 6. `torus_check.py` enumerates every perfect matching of the dual honeycomb torus, classifies each by crossing parity, and finds the four P(s, t) determinants reproduce the four class counts exactly, with the class (n mod 2, n mod 2) positive and the other three negative, and 2 N(n mod 2, n mod 2) equal to the transfer-matrix count. At n = 5 and 6 that count is 3630 and 263640, the values Krawczyk published, so matchings to parity classes to a published number closes end to end

rows.title: A bounded negative on PP(182)
rows.claim: A bounded negative on PP(182). The machines printing 181 or 183, the only counts a 182-printer could sit beside, number exactly 10, and that set is closed three ways: depth 1 over all 22,258 machines the searches have ever printed, and depth 2 over all 146 known witnesses in three chunks, each return the same 10 and nothing else. Depth 2 from those 10 gives no 182, flipping all 10 halting writes gives no 182, and depth 3 from the first of them gives no 182
rows.check: three independent harvests agree on the same 10 machines; every sweep deduped as it streamed
rows.literature: none
rows.status: 182 is structurally thinner than 178, whose straddle set held 52; depth 3 on the remaining 9 is the last space near it

rows.title: The straddle method, run against every open n below 260, closes none of them
rows.claim: The straddle method, run against every open n below 260, closes none of them. For each of 221, 222, 227, 228, 231, 232, 246, 248 and 251, the machines printing the counts either side were collected from a depth-2 sweep of all 146 witnesses and searched two changes out asking for that hole alone: all empty. 182 separately survives depth 3 from five of its ten straddlers and a 4,000,000-step random walk over 76 witnesses
